agent.problem: The answers mix different kinds of things: "truth" is an abstract concept, "Cain" is a person, and "Egypt" is a place. They are not the same kind of answer for "the way of ___."

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

agent.problem: Several choice cards rely on the preceding cards to identify their subject. Cards 2, 3, 5, 7, 8, 10, 12 and 17 use "these men" or bare pronouns without identifying the false teachers, so the questions do not consistently stand alone when the story card is no longer visible.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

agent.problem: The card cites only 2 Peter 2:14-15, but its identification of Balaam as a prophet comes from verse 16, which calls it "the prophet's madness." The citation does not cover everything the card tells.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.
